name: Gerlossteinbahn
kurzbeschreibung: The Gerlossteinbahn cable car at Hainzenberg in the Zillertal ascends to the sunny Gerlosstein plateau at 1,644 metres, featuring alpine meadows and the Almflieger zipline.
preis: Mountain plateau trails freely accessible; Gerlossteinbahn cable car fares apply
oeffnungszeiten: Summer operations daily late May to mid-October, 08:30 to 17:00
beschreibung:
Überblick

The time-honored Gerlossteinbahn aerial tramway, situated in the mountainside village of Hainzenberg above Zell am Ziller, unlocks the family-friendly alpine playground of the Gerlosstein plateau at 1,644 metres above sea level. Preserved as a tranquil, unhurried haven in contrast to the livelier resort hubs of the Zillertal, the Gerlosstein is an insider favorite for hikers who treasure unspoiled nature, blooming pastures, and expansive horizons. The classic cable car ascends along striking limestone crags, sweeping passengers onto a sun-drenched plateau within minutes. At the top terminal, an awe-inspiring vista unfurls across the entire Zillertal Valley, the Tux Alps, and the rugged glaciated crests of the Reichenspitz group. Charming alpine dairy chalets and thrilling mountain activities—such as the Almflieger aerial zipline—make the Gerlosstein one of the most rewarding mountain escapes in the Zillertal Arena. Besonders geschätzt wird das Gebiet für seine intakte alpine Kulturlandschaft und die herzliche Tiroler Gastfreundschaft auf den urigen Bergbauernhöfen.

Route & Anforderungen

The Gerlosstein recreation zone accommodates casual strollers as well as seasoned mountaineers. Radiating from the top cable car station, gentle stroller-accessible gravel paths loop across the pasturelands or lead on scenic excursions toward the Kotahornalm and Larchkopfalm huts (1 to 2 hours walking time, mild elevation changes). Ambitious alpine hikers can follow the steep rocky trail climbing to the prominent Gerlossteinwand peak (2,166 metres) or tackle the renowned Gerlossteinwand via ferrata (grade C/D, strictly for experienced climbers with full safety gear). Sneakers suffice for the high plateau promenades, whereas sturdy ankle-high trekking boots with vibram rubber soles are mandatory for traversing the crags to the summit.

Besuch & Anreise

Travel by car follows motorway A12 (exit Zillertal) along highway B169 to Zell am Ziller, ascending federal road B165 toward Gerlos to the Gerlossteinbahn valley station in Hainzenberg. Free visitor parking is available at the lift base. Rail passengers take the ÖBB train to Jenbach and switch to the scenic Zillertalbahn to Zell am Ziller, boarding local bus line 4094 heading to Gerlos, which stops directly in front of the cable car terminal.

Tipps

Experience the 'Almflieger Gerlosstein': this high-flying zipline system whisks riders along four distinct cable spans covering over two kilometres at speeds up to 50 km/h above the alpine meadows, pairing thrilling sensations with panoramic views over the valley.
